sections.title: Introduction
paragraphs: I put AI into practice, lead by example, and build with a product mindset. As a technical leader and product-minded software engineer, I connect deep engineering experience with a broad view of the product—from understanding the problem to delivery and continuous improvement.

sections.title: The person behind the code.
paragraphs: I’m a product-minded software engineer with 11+ years of professional experience, focused on practical AI and AI-assisted engineering.
With 5+ years in technical leadership, I lead by example, stay hands-on, and help teammates grow.
I connect user needs and business goals with delivery, taking ownership from discovery to improvement.
A T-shaped engineer, I combine engineering depth with breadth across the product lifecycle and strong attention to detail.

I hold a Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science and Engineering and am completing a Master’s degree in Internet Technologies and Cybersecurity at [FCSE - Ss. Cyril and Methodius University](https://finki.ukim.mk/en/) in Skopje.

Programming competitions are part of my engineering roots: RoboMac AI winner (2015); 3rd place, Macedonian National Competition in Informatics (2012); ACM ICPC, Bucharest (2015); Junior Balkan Olympiad in Informatics, Belgrade (2007); CodeFu finalist (2014–2019).

sections.title: Selected experience.
paragraphs: A few selected engagements from my career—not a complete work history. These examples span payment systems and dental software, with employers and clients shown separately.

items.title: Reliable payment systems
items.subtitle: Technical leadership & hands-on delivery
paragraphs: Building and evolving .NET payment solutions on a platform that processes billions of dollars annually. The work supports high-volume, mission-critical financial operations, where reliability, scalability, and safe releases matter.
Cross-functional delivery alongside engineering, QA, product, and architecture stakeholders.
bullets: Lead work from requirements and solution design through testing, release coordination, and post-release support.
Establish maintainable architecture, code quality, and testing practices.
Mentor engineers and collaborate with globally distributed teams.

items.title: Engineering in three dimensions
items.subtitle: Dental CAD/CAM software
paragraphs: Developed dental CAD/CAM software using .NET across Frame Design, Anatomy Design, and TRIOS, working with complex architectures and solving geometric problems in three dimensions.
bullets: Worked across three dental software products.
Developed algorithms for geometric problems in 3D space.
Applied algorithmic problem solving to complex dental-design workflows.

sections.title: What I bring to a team.
paragraphs: Practical AI, leadership by example, product thinking, and engineering depth shape how I work and support the people around me.

items.title: Put AI into practice
items.subtitle: Practical AI
paragraphs: Apply AI-assisted workflows to everyday engineering. Define clear intent, evaluate the output, and use engineering judgment to decide what to trust and ship.

items.title: Lead by example
items.subtitle: Hands-on leadership
paragraphs: Take ownership, stay hands-on, and demonstrate the standards I ask of others. Share context, give constructive feedback, and help teammates develop confidence and independence.

items.title: Start with the problem
items.subtitle: Product thinking
paragraphs: Understand users, question assumptions, and connect engineering decisions to meaningful product outcomes. Stay involved beyond implementation to see whether the work solves the problem.

items.title: Go deep. Connect the whole.
items.subtitle: T-shaped engineering
paragraphs: Combine engineering depth with breadth across discovery, architecture, development, testing, and delivery. Bring strong attention to detail to individual decisions and the product as a whole.

sections.title: From operational problem to maintained product.

items.title: Understand
items.subtitle: Find the right problem
paragraphs: Clarify users, business goals, constraints, and what success looks like. Use conversations and quick AI-assisted UI prototypes to test assumptions before committing to a solution.

items.title: Architect
items.subtitle: Give the solution structure
paragraphs: Turn the problem into clear requirements, boundaries, and acceptance criteria. Decide where AI can help and how its output will be evaluated.

items.title: Build
items.subtitle: Turn intent into working software
paragraphs: Work in small, reviewable increments, using AI agents with clear context and instructions. Stay hands-on with design, implementation, code review, and testing, and take responsibility for the result.

items.title: Launch & improve
items.subtitle: The release is a beginning
paragraphs: Validate behavior, release carefully, and learn using evidence from real users and production operation. Improve the product and the team’s workflow, sharing useful practices and lessons along the way.

sections.title: Built to learn. Shared to help.
paragraphs: A selection of personal projects built to explore ideas, solve everyday problems, and share what I learn. These projects predate my current focus on AI-assisted engineering.

items.title: Coding Problems
items.subtitle: A practical algorithms notebook
paragraphs: Python solutions and curated resources for learning algorithms and data structures. Written to make the ideas approachable across languages.

items.title: Virus Spreading
items.subtitle: Making an invisible problem visible
paragraphs: An interactive vanilla JavaScript simulation exploring how different parameters affect spreading and flattening the curve. An educational visualization, not an epidemiological prediction tool.

items.title: SlediPratki
items.subtitle: One place to follow a package
paragraphs: A Chrome extension built to track postal shipments in Macedonia, with background updates and notifications.

sections.title: Discipline, one step at a time.
paragraphs: Long-distance running—half-marathons and marathons—is how I practice discipline: showing up early in the morning or late in the evening, even when motivation is low.
Away from the run, I try to learn something new every day about AI, leadership, product development, or software engineering.

sections.title: Let's build something useful.
paragraphs: Have an interesting problem, a product idea, or a different perspective? I'd be happy to connect.
Based in Skopje, North Macedonia — CET/CEST (UTC+1 in winter, UTC+2 in summer). Strong overlap with European working hours · US Eastern mornings.
